chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) issued a judgment in a case of two men who claimed a mule. One of them presented two witnesses against his companion, and the other presented five. He judged that the owner of the five witnesses received five shares, and the owner of the two witnesses received two shares.
This is the end of the Book of Judgments and Rulings from the Book of Al-Kafi, and it is followed by the Book of Faith, Vows, and Expiations, if God Almighty wills.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali rule on disputes involving multiple witnesses?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) illustrates the principle of proportional compensation based on witness count, a unique jurisprudential approach often discussed in Shia legal theory regarding the weight of testimony. As the concluding hadith of the 'Miscellaneous' chapter in Al-Kafi, it serves as a bridge to the subsequent book on Oaths and Vows, highlighting the transition from judicial verdicts to personal religious obligations. This case underscores the flexibility of early Islamic jurisprudence in handling evidentiary disputes without requiring a fixed number of witnesses for validity.
